prompt: Which Windows console manages DNS zones and records?
options: DNS Manager (dnsmgmt.msc)
Disk Management (diskmgmt.msc)
Services alone (services.msc)
Local Users and Groups (lusrmgr.msc)
en: DNS Manager is the dedicated console for zones and resource records.
ru: DNS Manager zones aur resource records manage karne ki dedicated console hai.

prompt: What does a standard primary zone provide?
options: The writable authoritative copy for that zone
Only cached responses from public resolvers
Only a list of conditional-forwarder addresses
A read-only copy that must never be edited
en: Standard primary records are maintained at the writable authoritative source.
ru: Standard primary records writable authoritative source par maintain hotay hain.

prompt: What must exist for a zone to be stored in AD DS on this Windows DNS server?
options: A domain controller with the DNS Server role
A workgroup machine with only a matching DNS suffix
A Windows client with an SSH alias
A secondary zone file in any directory
en: AD-integrated zone storage requires the appropriate domain-controller DNS environment.
ru: AD-integrated storage ke liye munasib domain-controller DNS environment chahiye.

prompt: Where are standard Windows DNS zone files stored by default?
options: %windir%\System32\Dns
%windir%\System32\drivers\etc only
The client’s Downloads folder
The VMware virtual-network editor directory
en: File-backed zone data normally uses the DNS directory, distinct from the hosts file.
ru: File-backed zone data DNS directory mein hota hai; hosts file alag hai.

prompt: Which record associates a host name with an IPv4 address?
options: A
PTR
NS
SOA
en: An A record stores the IPv4 mapping for a DNS name.
ru: A record DNS naam ki IPv4 mapping store karta hai.

prompt: What does a CNAME record store?
options: A canonical target DNS name
The alias’s private signing key
The destination’s subnet mask
A replacement default gateway
en: A CNAME references another name; address resolution follows that target.
ru: CNAME doosray naam ko reference karta hai; address target se resolve hota hai.

prompt: Which record identifies an authoritative name server for a zone?
options: NS
PTR
MX
TXT
en: NS records describe the zone’s authoritative name-server names.
ru: NS records zone ke authoritative name-server names batate hain.

prompt: Which record includes a zone serial and refresh-related metadata?
options: SOA
A
CNAME
PTR
en: SOA publishes zone authority and version/timer information.
ru: SOA authority, version aur timers ki information publish karta hai.

prompt: What is the IPv4 reverse zone for the classroom 192.168.0.0/24 network?
options: 0.168.192.in-addr.arpa
192.168.0.in-addr.arpa
vcplab.com.in-addr.arpa
en: The /24 reverse zone reverses the three network octets under in-addr.arpa.
ru: /24 reverse zone mein teen network octets ulat kar in-addr.arpa ke saath aate hain.

prompt: What does allowing nonsecure dynamic updates imply?
options: Updates may be accepted without authenticated secure updating
Every update is automatically DNSSEC validated
Only domain administrators can ever submit updates
All client DNS traffic becomes encrypted
en: Nonsecure updating permits unauthenticated updates and is not a secure production default.
ru: Nonsecure updating unauthenticated updates allow karti hai; secure production default nahin.

prompt: DNS01 is a workgroup DNS server. Which wizard choice matches the recorded forward-zone design?
options: Standard primary, file-backed VCPLAB.Com
AD-integrated secondary VCPLAB.Com
A stub containing every writable host record
A conditional forwarder replacing all local records
en: The recorded classroom design used a standard primary, not AD-integrated storage.
ru: Recorded classroom design standard primary tha, AD-integrated storage nahin.

prompt: You create VCPLAB.Com successfully. What is still needed for address-to-name records?
options: Configure the appropriate reverse zone and PTR records
Rename the forward zone to a subnet mask
Convert every A record into a CNAME
Use the SSH config file as the reverse zone
en: Forward-zone creation does not itself create a reverse-zone record set.
ru: Forward zone banane se reverse-zone record set khud nahin banta.

prompt: Which A-record data matches the recorded DNS02 host?
options: dns02.vcplab.com → 192.168.0.122
dns02.vcplab.com → 192.168.0.121
dns02.vcplab.com → 192.168.0.123
dns02.vcplab.com → 19.168.0.122
en: The classroom address assigned to DNS02 is .122.
ru: Classroom mein DNS02 ka assigned address .122 hai.

prompt: A draft DNS03 A record shows 19.168.0.123. What correction matches the classroom network?
options: Correct the address to 192.168.0.123
Leave it because DNS ignores missing digits
Change the zone to 19.in-addr.arpa
Change all other machines to match the draft typo
en: The recorded typo omitted a digit; the intended host address is 192.168.0.123.
ru: Recorded typo mein digit missing tha; intended host IP 192.168.0.123 hai.

prompt: For dns.vcplab.com to alias DNS01, which CNAME target is appropriate?
options: dns01.vcplab.com
0.168.192.in-addr.arpa
en: The alias references DNS01’s canonical host name, not its literal address.
ru: Alias DNS01 ke canonical host name ko reference karta hai, literal IP ko nahin.

prompt: Which query directly tests the classroom DNS alias through DNS01?
options: nslookup dns.vcplab.com. 192.168.0.121
nslookup dns01.vcplab.com. 192.168.0.121
nslookup vcplab.com. 192.168.0.121
en: The queried name must be the alias; other names do not directly test it.
ru: Query mein alias ka naam chahiye; doosray names alias ko directly test nahin karte.

prompt: The dns01 A record exists. You select Update associated pointer (PTR) record. What condition matters?
options: The appropriate reverse zone must be available for the PTR operation
An SSH alias must exist for every DNS name
The forward zone must first be deleted
The IP must be entered into the CNAME field
en: Associated PTR creation depends on an appropriate reverse-zone configuration and successful operation.
ru: Associated PTR ke liye munasib reverse-zone configuration aur successful operation chahiye.

prompt: A forward query for DNS02 succeeds through DNS01. What does that prove?
options: DNS01 answered the DNS02 name mapping for that query
DNS02’s secondary service has definitely been tested
An application on DNS02 accepts all connections
DNS02 has joined Active Directory
en: Querying a host’s name through DNS01 does not test the named host’s own DNS service.
ru: DNS01 se host ka naam poochna us named host ki apni DNS service ka test nahin.

prompt: The reverse view appears empty immediately after an update. What is a sensible first action?
options: Refresh the console and inspect existing records before adding duplicates
Delete and recreate every zone immediately
Disable all network adapters
Change every host’s address without checking
en: A stale console view can mislead; inspect refreshed state before editing data.
ru: Stale console view misleading ho sakti hai; edit se pehle refreshed state dekhein.

prompt: The isolated VMnet2 lab uses .121/.122/.123 with a blank gateway. Which statement is accurate?
options: Same-subnet DNS queries do not require Internet access
Every local lookup requires a public DNS server
Blank gateway proves local DNS cannot work
A gateway automatically creates the forward zone
en: Same-subnet traffic can reach a local DNS server without an Internet route.
ru: Same-subnet traffic Internet route ke baghair local DNS server tak ja sakti hai.

prompt: A query for dns02.vcplab.com returns NXDOMAIN from DNS01. What should be checked first?
options: The exact queried name, selected server, zone and expected record
The ESXi datastore capacity alone
The browser’s saved application password alone
The Windows wallpaper setting
en: NXDOMAIN is a negative DNS reply; check naming and hosted data before unrelated changes.
ru: NXDOMAIN negative DNS reply hai; pehle naming aur hosted data check hon.

prompt: DNS01 displays Server: Unknown, yet returns a correct forward answer. What might explain the display?
options: Its server-IP reverse name is missing or unavailable
The successful A answer proves no DNS service exists
The CNAME must be changed into a subnet mask
Every forward record must be deleted
en: The resolver’s reverse display name is separate from the requested forward answer.
ru: Resolver ka reverse display naam requested forward answer se alag hai.

prompt: The record exists, but queries time out from a client. Which investigation is most relevant?
options: Check the client path, DNS service/listening address and permitted DNS traffic
Assume the record must be a CNAME
Recreate the zone as an AD domain immediately
Change capitalization of every name as the only fix
en: A timeout concerns lack of timely response; data presence alone does not establish reachability.
ru: Timeout timely response na milna hai; data maujood hona reachability ka proof nahin.

prompt: Reverse entries point to DNS02.vcplab.com and dns02.vcplab.com for the same IP. What does capitalization imply?
options: The target names are equivalent because DNS names are case-insensitive
They necessarily identify two different domains
The lowercase target is always invalid
The uppercase target disables reverse queries
en: Capitalization alone does not distinguish DNS names. Inspect and remove redundant entries carefully if appropriate.
ru: Sirf capitals se DNS names alag nahin hotay; redundant entries ki safai carefully hoti hai.

prompt: Querying vcplab.com gives no A answer while dns01.vcplab.com resolves. What is a valid explanation?
options: The zone apex may lack an A record even though the host record exists
A zone must return every host’s IP when its apex is queried
The host answer proves the reverse zone is corrupt
Every successful host lookup automatically creates an apex A record
en: A zone name and a host name are distinct record owners; not every zone apex has an A record.
ru: Zone name aur host name alag record owners hain; har zone apex par A lazmi nahin.
